checks: Checked 19899b61b9ca5f3a §§5–8, (16)–(25), and the exact same-wave quantile predecessor. The old cut at β=0 crosses the appropriate triangular-slice edges away from the vertices, is transverse on the crossed facets, and has c′_0=0. One-dimensional integration across each facet gives the positive sign v(t−t_0)/a_{iF} in the angular derivative. This proves the finite limit when R_0=0.

The parabolic top erosion gives speed ||X||² on the top facet only. The exact triangle moments are total 9/2 and mean cap integral 16/9; scaling by (1+ε)^4 and subtracting (4/9)D gives −(2/9)(1+ε)^4. The reciprocal-tilt fixed-cap response therefore diverges to minus infinity.

For i=1 the coarea uses dX_2 dt and interval length 2r−b with centroid −b/2. The quantile equation gives ∫b²=8c_β. Direct integration yields horizontal moments (−4c_β,2c_β) and vertical moment 2t_0c_β+(2A/3)β. The vertex permutations are volume-preserving and act contragrediently on the normals, so the other coarea moments follow.

For fixed convex K, first mass variation of the cap is B_i·M_i−S_βN_i·(ξ,h), hence these signs reverse for the loss. Weighted horizontal mark terms cancel, S_0=4 supplies +4gh, and the vertical normal term is −(2gA/9)ΣB_{i,t}(0). A fixed-normal retune adds S_β times its threshold velocity, giving the stated opposite of the old level-corrected loss.

The section outward normal in the clipped body is −N_i/||N_i||, so the section fluxes are −c_βS_β and −βS_β. Thus the body-boundary homothety loss is 3Q+(c_β−aβ)S_β; R′_0=−4a, and the mark and threshold motions cancel it at each tilt. The two actual convex example paths are unaffected by the missing general motion hypothesis.

With compact convex K_e and Hausdorff error δ, support functions differ by at most δ on unit normals. If x+δB⊂K then u·x≤h_K(u)−δ≤h_{K_e}(u) for every unit u, giving inner containment. Outer containment K_e⊂K+δB follows from Hausdorff distance. Thus the symmetric difference lies in the old boundary strip. The fixed-tilt cap strip intersects the neighborhoods of its finitely many crossed facets transversely, giving O(e²) volume, while the other facets have positive distance from the section. The separated first variations therefore add as claimed.

issues.defect: Hausdorff distance controls containment in outer parallel neighborhoods, but without convexity does not confine K_e symmetric-difference K to a strip along the old boundary. A thin interior slit or sheet can have thickness O(e) and leave the set Hausdorff-close while its removed volume lies in the moving-cap strip far from the body boundary. The asserted O(e²) cross-term estimate therefore does not follow from the named Hausdorff condition alone.
issues.locator: Statement paragraph beginning “At a fixed β” and proof paragraph beginning “For a fixed β”
issues.repair: Require the moving K_e to be compact convex bodies, in addition to the stated fixed-cap first variations and O(|e|) Hausdorff distance. Then support-function comparison gives inner and outer parallel containment and confines the symmetric difference to an O(|e|) old-boundary strip. The transverse finite facet intersections give the required O(e²) cross term.

initial_review.readability: The response is in raw level-corrected units. The mark and normal terms survive the reciprocal tilt, and retuning is a distinct operation.
initial_review.summary: The frustum moment, boundary signs and homothety cancellation check. The moving-body superposition needs the intended convexity of K_e, or explicit equivalent boundary-strip control, to justify its Hausdorff argument.

readability: The revised statement explicitly separates the facewise response for a speed from its use on an actual moving convex body with the named first losses and Hausdorff control.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The revised moving-body hypothesis and support-function argument give the needed O(e²) cross-term bound at each fixed tilt. The exact boundary moments and motion signs are unchanged.
